page.title: Why tinyactors exists
page.description: tinyactors exists so that every system can be modeled as a statechart, in every environment, at a cost small enough to model everything.

hero.headline: Model every system as a statechart
hero.lede: I built tinyactors to use statecharts everywhere I write code: Node.js, Bun, Python, a browser and C.
hero.author: Dario Hamidi

section.heading: Statecharts changed how I build
section.p: A statechart puts an actor's logic in one chart and keeps its side effects outside it.
It is a formal model, so I can reason about a chart, and so can an agent.

section.heading: Ten years of ideas pointed here
section.p: Event sourcing and command sourcing taught me to model a system as a stream of events.
Statecharts showed me the step they left out: model the system itself as a reactive system.

section.heading: Every system can be reactive
section.p: A program written in a functional, logic or imperative style can always be modeled as a reactive system.
Most systems built today already are one: they wait for an event, then respond. Picking that as the base abstraction fits the work.

section.heading: No runtime ran them everywhere
section.p: Once I saw this, I wanted statecharts in every program I write.
JavaScript had XState, but nothing ran one chart the same way in every language I use.

section.heading: So I built one core for all
section.p: tinyactors runs the W3C's statechart language from one C core, and every language binds that same core.

claim.p: It runs your actors on your own event loop, in Node.js, Bun, Python, a browser or C.

claim.statement: It passes the W3C's own tests
claim.p: tinyactors passes all 191 automatic tests of the W3C suite, and every binding runs the same suite.

section.heading: Small enough to model everything
section.p: An actor costs so little that every user, session, order or device can have a chart of its own.

claim.p: That is a started actor in Node.js, measured with a million in one process.

claim.statement: A sleeping actor keeps about 120 bytes
claim.p: Idle actors hibernate to your store and wake on their next event.
claim.source: Twice the actors, the same cost

section.p: That is the freedom I wanted: no part of a system too small to get its own chart.
